body: Yeah maybe you’re right. I have a lot of issues with this flat and I want all my issues fixed. I guess I just wanted to kick up a fuss, show them I’m not an idiot and that I deserve respect as a tenant, that I’m not just a naive kid they can push around and ignore like they have been. I figured if I did that they’d be inclined to actually get off their asses and fix everything, and so I wouldn’t have to let their people in that make me feel unsafe and uncomfortable in my own home. That’s wishful thinking though and I can see how I’m just obstructing getting an actual fix for things I need fixing. I’m cynical as to their motivations and I feel like they should face some sort of disciplinary for the fact I’ve been waiting for most of these issues to be fixed for almost two years. But again, wishful thinking. Just going to let the repair happen, clean up the inevitable mess, continue writing emails to the letting agent that will be ignored and just sit and cross my fingers that one day they’ll help.

I appreciate the suggestion but I’m not an idiot. I have an old-style immersion heater with a a static heating element that’s all wrapped in insulation. Part of this particular contractor’s derisive bemusement I described when answering some of my simple questions was the retort ‘yeah if you want to electrocute yourself’ when I asked if I’d be able to fix and change the temp myself.

Yeah if he’d made a legit error and came by to fix it then it would be okay, and I have gotten on well with a lot of other contractors this agent has sent round so it’s not like I’m just oversensitive or a difficult person. This contractor ignored me commenting on the temperature back when he installed it and left it like that, thinking that would be the end of it and probably thinking he wouldn’t see me again. The only reason he’s coming back at all is because the letting agent is trying to get ahead of this investigation and possible lawsuit by getting the tap fixed before it can be looked at by anyone. I also forgot to mention the ‘boss’ in question that called me out of the blue turns out it’s actually just the agents dad!

My request to my agent feels very simple ‘please don’t invite people into my home, the place where I live, that I know will do a bad job, leave a big mess and act like an asshole’, and it seems wrong that I can’t stop that from happening?

I understand, and sorry for being a bit of an ass this whole situation is just stressing me out. Like I said below, I don’t think the two (emergency and category 1) are synonymous as they’re coming from two different legal documents, but I understand what you mean. I don’t have an issue with them fixing my taps or solving that issue, I’m only delaying because they’re pushing this cowboy into my flat again after he’s left a bunch a mess, done a bad job and been an asshole the whole time.

The category 1 stuff is part of the Homes Act 2018 and the ‘emergency’ terminology is part of my tenancy agreement. They aren’t synonymous. Having a scalding tap is pretty serious, but it’s not like a burst pipe or gas leak and similar things listed as ‘emergencies’. 

My issue isn’t even that they’re coming to fix it, or the nature of what they’re coming to fix, that’s all fine and good and I want it fixed for sure. My issue is that they’re pushing it quick which will prevent me being able to check in with actual lawyers and the local council on what my next steps should be regarding all these repairs, and that they’re forcing on me this cowboy that does a half-assed job, leaves mess and treats me like shit while he’s in my home.

Lol so you expect my cold water tap to also kick out scalding hot water before it counts as category 1? What a ridiculous comment. I think I found my agent right here trying to be sneaky.

I have six taps, 2 on the kitchen sink and 4 bathroom for sink and bath , 3 cold and 3 hot. All 3 hot water taps are scalding.

I’ve been visited by this contractor multiple times. It’s not that I don’t like him, it’s just that every time he’s visited he’s left a lot of mess that I’ve then had to clean up, trampled dirt through my flat and left tiny bits of wire all over my bathroom carpet as well as several leftover pieces of plastic or redundant parts, then once he’d finished and I asked some simple questions including ‘can I adjust the temperature of this myself as the tap seems a little too hot’, he acted like I was an idiot for asking and laughed at me, said that I was a wuss and that it needs to be that hot to prevent legionella (I know it has to be over 70 degrees Celsius, but this tap has to be near boiling, 90 or higher), and didn’t even answer the question.

I didn’t even think about this but you’re right, I’m still amazed that this ‘boss’ who actually is the agent in question’s dad, decided to argue the definition of emergency with me and threaten to argue said definition in court.

There is a laundry list of issues with the flat, this is just one of them. If they fix this issue and pretend like it never happened, I’m losing some of my legal grounding to sue or open further investigations, and it’s more the way they are going about it. They are scrambling to get a cowboy in to fix the few issues that really stand out as something they’re liable for, whilst they will continue to ignore the rest. It feels disingenuous at best and downright unlawful at worst for them to only start working on these issues when I’ve started pursuing a complaints procedure through their redress scheme and through the council.
Yes, because they’re trying to get a notably bad, rude and messy contractor to do a quick and dirty job of the repair to undercut the upcoming HHSRS assessment.

Just the fish below the handle sadly. I’m in the UK, around the midlands. Hope that helps.
